body.x: TOKYO, Japan (AVING Special Report on 'CEATEC JAPAN 2006') -- <Visual News> The screen size competition took place between Korean companies, namely Samsung and LG and at CES 2006 in Las Vegas this January Panasonic claimed to have the most advanced technology by launching a 103-inch PDP TV, an inch bigger than the previous largest screen manufactured by a Korean company.

Furthermore, at IFA 2006 in Berlin last September, JVC exhibited a 110-inch Projection TV, thus indicating that the competition of who can make the biggest screen hasn''t stopped in the industry. At CEATEC 2006 Panasonic and JVC presented a 103-inch PDP TV and a 110-inch Projection TV respectively drawing a large group of people''s attention.
It is a general consensus among the industry experts that the screen quality is about the same even though there is a difference between a ''Projection TV'' and a ''PDP TV'' in the manufacturing.

A member of JVC emphasizes on the fact that a 110-inch Projection TV requires only 230W power source, indicating that the recent large PDP TV has disadvantages of generating high heat and requiring high power.
< AVING Special Report Team for ''CEATEC 2006'': Publisher & Editor, Kevin Choi, Benjamin Oh, Jason Lee, Phoebe Kwon, Sheri Choi, Daniel Sirh, Rose Kim >
